Anthropic is expanding Claude Cowork from desktop to the web and mobile.

•	The beta will roll out gradually on select paid plans.

•	It starts with the Max plan, with more plans to follow.

•	Claude Cowork will be available on iPhone, iPad, Android, and claude.ai.

•	Anthropic says Cowork can work across files, calendar, email, messaging apps, the web, and connected tools.

•	Scheduled tasks can run even when no device is online.

•	If Claude needs a human decision, it will ask on your phone.

•	Anthropic will extend doubled Cowork usage limits through August 5.

Why it matters: this makes Claude more useful as a background work assistant that can keep moving across devices.

BlackRock has launched the iShares Nasdaq-100 ETF ($IQQ), set to begin trading on July 9.

•	The fund tracks the Nasdaq-100 Index.

•	It targets companies across technology, healthcare, consumer discretionary, and communications services.

•	Initial NAV is $24 per share.

•	The gross expense ratio is 0.12%, temporarily cut to 0.10% through July 31, 2027.

•	It enters competition with Invesco’s QQQ products and State Street’s Nasdaq-100 fund.

•	BlackRock already oversees more than $41 billion across existing Nasdaq-focused ETFs.

Why it matters: BlackRock is using a cheaper Nasdaq-100 fund to tap AI-driven demand for megacap growth exposure.

Netflix ($NFLX) is expanding into publisher video content starting August 3.

•	The company signed licensing deals with PMX (Penske Media, including Variety, Rolling Stone, Billboard), BuzzFeed Studios, Condé Nast, Hearst Magazines, People Inc., and Tastemade.

•	Content ranges from 2 minutes to 20+ minutes per episode.

•	Coverage spans travel, food, fashion, celebrity, and lifestyle topics.

•	The rollout covers the U.S., Canada, U.K., Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand.

Why it matters: Netflix is diversifying beyond scripted and unscripted originals by tapping established publisher brands for short-form and mid-length content.

Amazon’s $25 billion bond sale is pressuring tech credit.

•	Investors sold existing hyperscaler bonds to make room for Amazon’s new issue.

•	The move pushed outstanding hyperscaler debt lower on Tuesday.

•	The sale signals fatigue over the wave of AI financings.

•	Amazon is seeking at least $25 billion in eight tranches.

•	The offering could grow if demand is strong.

Why it matters: Big AI funding deals are starting to crowd the credit market, even for highly rated tech borrowers.

$ACN — Accenture wins a NATO digital infrastructure contract

•	Accenture signed a €200 million contract with NATO’s Communications and Information Agency.

•	The deal runs for seven years.

•	Accenture will partner with Leonardo.

•	The contract covers NATO’s Protected Business Network.

•	It will support about 29,000 users across NATO.

•	The platform is cloud-enabled and built for secure digital operations.

Why it matters: The contract gives Accenture a long-term NATO role in secure cloud infrastructure and digital resilience.

Figma $FIG acquires the team behind Bud.

•	Figma acquired the team behind the vibe coding and AI agent platform Bud.

•	Bud will shut down on Jul. 18.

•	Users must migrate projects by then.

•	Bud started as Orchids and let users spin up apps for mobile, web, Slack, browser, and more.

•	It later became an agent platform that can browse the web, access services, write code, and automate tasks.

•	Figma has been adding more AI and moving coding and prototyping closer to its canvas.

Why it matters: Figma is trying to move beyond design into app building and prototyping.

Perplexity says it plans to use Nvidia’s new CPU.

•	Perplexity confirmed it plans to use Nvidia’s Vera CPU.

•	Nvidia expects $20 billion in sales from Vera by the end of this fiscal year.

•	Nvidia is pitching Vera as a broader computing chip, not just an AI chip.

•	Perplexity said Vera fits its core AI agent workloads.

•	Perplexity said Vera handled coding tasks about 1.5x faster than traditional CPUs.

•	Perplexity did not disclose how many CPUs it plans to buy.

•	Nvidia has said OpenAI, Anthropic, and Oracle also plan to use its CPUs.

Why it matters: Nvidia is trying to expand beyond AI GPUs into the CPU market, while Perplexity is backing hardware built for AI agents.
